what: The audit that makes 'convert all known workflows to BDD' a bounded, checkable claim. Each entry is an upstream *universe* of workflows (a directory in another repo) and how this repo's BDD corpus accounts for every workflow inside it: `ported` maps an upstream name to the BDD feature that is its decision-graph port; `search_space` names a workflow that is deliberately NOT ported, with the reason (an optimizer search-space, not a decision policy, so a BDD decision graph would have to invent the policy). `ported_all` means the whole universe is a 1:1 BDD port whose closure is proven by `bdd port-check`. `bdd scope-check` reads this file; `bdd scope-check --sources <ole-eval root>` puts it on trial against a live checkout (the listed names must equal the .py files on disk, so a new upstream workflow cannot be silently skipped). `enumerate: false` marks a universe whose upstream is not publicly enumerable (its names are pinned here and every ported feature is still existence-checked; `--sources` cannot list such an upstream, so it does not demand a directory for it).

universes.note: 66 deterministic guard scenarios, every one a @decision graph under bdd/workflows/ole_eval/ with its dsl/ole_eval/ spec; the closure is proven by `bdd port-check --cat ole_eval --pin bench/bdd/port_pins/ole_eval.json`.

universes.kind: mixed (one decision state-machine + a family of optimizer search-spaces)

search_space.anomaly_detection: optimizer search-space over (window, z_threshold, method, fill); eval_fn scores against ground truth, there is no deterministic policy to encode
search_space.c_program_runner: search-space over (program, input_value) where program is a compiled C/WASM artifact; the correct pick is data-dependent
search_space.data_cleaning: search-space over (program, input_offset) choosing a per-column C cleaning program; the program is discovered, not ruled
search_space.data_cleaning_columnar: column-level variant of data_cleaning; same search-space shape
search_space.data_cleaning_multistep: multi-step (12 cols x 2 steps) variant of data_cleaning; same search-space shape
search_space.data_cleaning_real: real-CSV variant with an LLM proposer; the proposer is the (learned) policy, so there is no fixed decision graph
search_space.label_stability: optimizer search-space over (window, similarity_threshold, consensus); no deterministic policy
search_space.outlier_detect: optimizer search-space over (window, threshold, fill); no deterministic policy
search_space.wasm_action_picker: search-space over (action, window, threshold, low, high); the action is looked up in a shared registry and the correct pick is data-dependent

universes.note: `agent_permission` is a permission state-machine + calibrated risk gate, so it IS a decision graph and was ported (P79). The other nine are parameter search-spaces for the LLM-as-optimizer loop; porting them would mean inventing a policy, so they are named here, with reasons, rather than forced into the decision vocabulary.

universes.upstream: agent-toolbox repo (skills/ + code/scripts/ + .githooks/; private - a set of shell/Python ops scripts, not a public workflow directory)
universes.note: The agent-toolbox decision workflows were ported to DSL first (dsl/agents/, whose README maps each spec to its upstream ops script) and then to BDD (@decision). Their upstream is a private repo of shell/Python scripts, so it cannot be enumerated publicly; the upstream names are pinned here and every ported feature must exist and be a @decision graph. `enumerate: false` tells `--sources` not to demand a directory - there is no public one to list - so the universe is accounted for by name instead of being silently omitted from the bound.
